member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.Calibration.BaselineSkew
member.summary: How far a pitch or roll prism baseline lies off its axis, and the error that puts into the angle computes from it. The computation is exact for a baseline in the vertical plane of its axis (fore-aft for pitch, port-starboard for roll). Off that plane it reads a constant bias when the prisms differ in height, and the other attitude axis leaks into the computed angle.
member.param: The angle in the VRF between the CP1 → CP2 baseline and the vertical plane of its axis: zero for an aligned baseline, 90° for one across the axis.
The angle computed for a level vessel, which reads straight into the C-O. For roll it is measured against gravity roll, which is what the prisms give (see ).
The computed angle's change per degree of the other axis, in degrees per degree, signed: per degree of roll (starboard down) for pitch, per degree of pitch (bow up) for roll.

member.summary: The skew of the CP1 → CP2 baseline for , from prism positions stored in GEOdc Standard axes (+X forward, +Y starboard, +Z down). Returns null when either prism is null or the prisms coincide. It also returns null for heading, because on a level vessel the heading computation subtracts the baseline's bearing exactly.
member.remarks: The errors come from running the computation on simulated world positions: the prism vector is rotated by a known Tate-Bryant attitude (R = Ry(pitch) · Rx(roll), heading north), then compared with the true angle. The cross-axis error is the central difference over ±1° of the other axis.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.Calibration.CalibrationComputer
member.summary: Derives computed angles from control-point positions. World positions are Easting, Northing and Height (a position series' A, B and C). VRF prism offsets are stored GEOdc Standard positions (+X forward, +Y starboard, +Z down).
member.remarks: Heading is the grid bearing of the CP1 → CP2 baseline less its bearing relative to the bow. Pitch and roll are the baseline's tilt from horizontal less its tilt in the VRF, taken along the baseline's fore-aft (pitch) or port-starboard (roll) direction, so they hold whichever way the vessel is heading. Results follow the GEOdc Standard convention: heading clockwise, pitch bow up, roll starboard down.

member.summary: The computed angle for each matched CP1/CP2 position pair, keyed by the CP1 row: the baseline's world angle less , plus and, for heading, . Heading wraps into [0°, 360°); pitch and roll into [−180°, 180°).
member.param: CP1 and CP2 world positions as (Easting, Northing, Height) in metres.
The attitude axis to compute.
The surveyor's baseline correction, added to every computed angle.
Added to every computed heading; must be null for pitch and roll.
The prisms' baseline angle in the VRF from ; zero when the prisms are not bound.
member.exception: is set for a capability other than heading.

member.summary: The CP1 → CP2 baseline's world angle for : its grid bearing for heading, or its elevation above horizontal, measured towards the same end as , for pitch and roll.

member.summary: The VRF prisms' CP1 → CP2 baseline angle for the capability: its bearing from the bow for heading, its rise towards the bow for pitch, or its rise towards port for roll, from prism positions stored in GEOdc Standard axes. default(Angle) (zero) when either position is null.

member.name: M:geoDC.Domain.Calibration.CalibrationComputer.ReadVrfBaseline(geoDC.Domain.Calibration.AngleSensorCapability,geoDC.Measurements.Angle)
member.summary: Converts from into the value the operator reads, whichever prism is CP1. For heading it is the bearing from the bow in [0°, 360°), clockwise. For pitch it is the baseline's tilt in [−90°, 90°], positive when the forward prism is higher. For roll it is the tilt, positive when the port prism is higher. The computation measures the world elevation from the same end, so this is the tilt it subtracts.

member.summary: The C-O for each computed angle that pairs with an observed one at : computed minus observed plus , wrapped into [−180°, 180°) and keyed by the computed row. Every input is GEOdc Standard: the computed angles from , the observed angles through , and the existing correction as stored, so the result is a GEOdc Standard correction. When the observed roll comes with its pitch, each computed gravity roll is first converted to Euler roll with the pitch of the observed row it pairs with (see ).

member.summary: The computed angles as differences them. A computed roll is the prism baseline's tilt from horizontal, which is gravity roll. When the roll comes with its pitch (), each computed row that pairs with an observed row is converted to Euler roll with that row's pitch, and rows with no pair are left out. Otherwise the computed angles are returned unchanged.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.Calibration.CalibrationCycle
member.summary: Reads where a job's calibration/verification cycle stands from the workflow states of its attempts and the outcomes of its verifications. Each sensor axis (an installation and one heading, pitch or roll capability) runs its own cycle.

member.name: M:geoDC.Domain.Calibration.CalibrationCycle.AwaitsVerification(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{geoDC.Domain.Calibration.CalibrationCycleCalibration},System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{geoDC.Domain.Calibration.CalibrationCycleVerification})
member.summary: Returns whether the next step for at least one sensor axis is a verification: the axis's most recent calibration is finalised, the only state that can be verified, and no verification of that calibration has a result yet.
member.remarks: The most recent calibration of an axis is the one created last among the calibrations of the same installation and capability, with the attempt identity breaking ties. Only that calibration can ask for verification. Earlier calibrations of the axis do not, whether or not they were verified. A verification still in progress leaves its calibration waiting. Calibrations with no target installation are ignored.

member.name: M:geoDC.Domain.Calibration.CalibrationCycle.AwaitsRecalibration(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{geoDC.Domain.Calibration.CalibrationCycleCalibration},System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{geoDC.Domain.Calibration.CalibrationCycleVerification})
member.summary: Returns whether the next step for at least one sensor axis is a recalibration after a failed verification. That is the case when the axis's most recent calibration has a calculated or finalised result, and the latest verification of it that has both a result and a pass or fail outcome failed.
member.remarks: The most recent calibration of an axis is chosen as for , so once a recalibration exists the failed verification of its predecessor no longer asks for one.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.Common.ContentHash
member.summary: Builds a deterministic SHA-256 over named content parts, for change detection on revisioned records. The hash covers content only. Callers leave out timestamps, authors and ids, so the same coordinates and metadata hash the same whoever entered them and whenever. Parts are written in the order given, as name=value lines with a canonical, culture-invariant rendering of each value. Callers must therefore add parts in a fixed order, not in dictionary order. Values are escaped, so a newline inside a value cannot forge another part or collide with the literal characters \\n.

member.name: M:geoDC.Domain.Common.Conventions.RollConversion.DifferenceBound(geoDC.Measurements.Angle,geoDC.Measurements.Angle)
member.summary: The largest difference between the two definitions for a gravity roll of magnitude up to at pitch magnitudes up to : the error a roll C-O can carry when gravity roll is compared as if it were Euler roll. The gap r − g, with r = asin(sin g / cos p), grows with both magnitudes (roughly tan g · p² / 2). Where the pitch reaches the inverse conversion's limit (|sin g| ≥ cos p) the Euler roll can be up to 90°, so the bound is 90° − g.
member.exception: is 90° or beyond.

member.summary: The exported value is a correction value: the C-O (Computed minus Observed), which answers "what value does the sensor need to add in order to read correctly?". It is added to the sensor's readings to give the VRF angle. The user-facing label is "Correction value".

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.Common.Primitives.COSemantics.MountAngle
member.summary: The exported value is a mount angle, which answers "what angle is the sensor actually mounted at, relative to the VRF?". The receiving software subtracts it from the measurements to give the VRF angle, so it is the negation of the correction value in the same convention. Kongsberg MRU, for example, asks for the value this way.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.Common.Primitives.RigidTransform
member.summary: A rigid (distance- and angle-preserving) transform of positions: p′ = R·p + t, with a proper rotation about the origin followed by the translation t in metres. The mapping direction is always current coordinates → transformed coordinates. Scale, shear, reflection, and perspective cannot be represented.

remarks.para: Numeric convention (rigid-v1): the rotation is a row-major 3×3 matrix of IEEE-754 doubles applied to column vectors, and the translation is in decimal metres rounded to places. Each rotated coordinate is computed in double precision and rounded half-to-even to places, then the translation is added exactly in decimal. A pure translation stays in decimal arithmetic throughout. The same stored transform and inputs therefore always produce the same coordinates.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.Common.Primitives.ZyxAngles
member.summary: A rotation as three angles in coordinate terms, applied about X first, then Y, then Z: the rotation is R = Rz(AboutZ) · Ry(AboutY) · Rx(AboutX). Each angle follows the matrix convention of about its positive coordinate axis, so a positive angle about Z turns +X toward +Y, about Y turns +Z toward +X, and about X turns +Y toward +Z. This holds regardless of the physical directions of the axes, so a display can state the sign without assuming a handedness. In the VRF, X is longitudinal, Y transverse and Z vertical, so the three are heading, pitch and roll.

member.summary: A reference is Missing, so the CRS is not known.

member.summary: A reference is Unspecified, which only a comparison can interpret, by assuming the other side's CRS.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.Crs.CoordinateTransformRefusalReason.UnknownDefinition
member.summary: The definition is neither in the catalogue nor an authority code PROJ knows.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.Crs.CoordinateTransformRefusalReason.LabelOnlyDefinition
member.summary: The catalogue has the definition as a label only, with no WKT2 for PROJ to read.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.Crs.CoordinateTransformRefusalReason.UnsupportedCrs
member.summary: PROJ describes the definition as something geoDC cannot transform, such as a bound or temporal CRS.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.Crs.CoordinateTransformRefusalReason.CoordinateKindMismatch
member.summary: A coordinate's kind does not match the source CRS, e.g. projected values for a geographic CRS.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.Crs.CoordinateTransformRefusalReason.MissingEpoch
member.summary: A dynamic CRS is involved and a coordinate has no epoch, so PROJ would silently assume one.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.Crs.CoordinateTransformRefusalReason.EpochMismatch
member.summary: The target reference states an epoch the coordinates are not at. Moving positions between epochs needs a velocity model, which a transformation does not apply.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.Crs.CoordinateTransformRefusalReason.NoStrictPath
member.summary: PROJ has only ballpark transformations between the CRSs. Often this is because a grid it needs is not installed.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.Crs.CoordinateTransformRefusalReason.TransformFailed
member.summary: A coordinate could not be transformed: PROJ failed on it, or it lies outside the area of use of the transformation PROJ would apply, because no transformation between the CRSs covers it.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.Crs.CoordinateTransformRefusalReason.EpochNotPreserved
member.summary: A transformed coordinate came back at a different epoch than it went in, so a time-dependent step may have used the wrong one.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.Crs.CoordinateTransformRefusalReason.ProjUnavailable
member.summary: The shipped PROJ library could not be loaded on this machine.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.DataSeriesAlignmentAnalyzer
member.summary: Previews how two series pair under a match configuration, and searches a bounded grid for the time offset that pairs the most rows. Both read the row snapshots they are given and change nothing: the operator decides whether to correct a dataset's timestamps or set an attempt's match offset.
member.remarks: Matching goes through with the reference as series A and the compared series as B, as a calibration, verification or GNSS check matches them. Excluded rows do not take part. Each row is keyed as stored rows are (), so timestamps are the effective ones and a dataset whose timestamps were corrected is previewed already corrected.

member.name: M:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.DataSeriesColumnDescriptor.CanCompareValuesWith(geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.DataSeriesColumnDescriptor)
member.summary: Whether this column's values can be overlaid on, or compared with, 's as the same quantity. Both columns need the same meaning in the same known unit. Angles also need the same known attitude axis and wrap range, and both conventions must be known and agree on that axis's positive direction, because stored angles are in their import convention and two conventions can reverse each other's sign. Roll also needs the same roll definition. A result column has no known unit, so it compares with nothing. Comparing timestamps does not need compatible values.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.DataSeriesEdit
member.summary: An append-only record of one logical edit to a data series' rows: what kind of edit it was and its parameters, who made it, when and why, and each changed row's fields before and after. The series' current rows already hold the result, so reading a series does not replay its history. Records are numbered from 1 within their series and are not edited or deleted once saved. Undoing a saved edit records a that points at it.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.DataSeriesEdit.MaxReasonLength
member.summary: The longest reason an edit records, after trimming.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.DataSeriesEdit.MaxTagLength
member.summary: The longest analysis tag an edit records, after trimming.

Records an edit with at least one patch, each changing at least one field. The parameters must fit the kind. A value edit must give its column, and no other kind may. A time shift must give its shift in seconds, and only a value edit or a time shift may give a value. A tag edit must give its tag, and no other kind may. A reversal must give the edit it reverses, and no other kind may. Throws when the parameters do not fit, and for an ordinal below 1, an unknown kind, or a reason or tag that is too long.

member.summary: A signed duration added to every timestamp of a data series, correcting an instrument clock that was off by a fixed amount: +90 s turns 12:00:00 into 12:01:30. member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.DataSeriesValueStatistics
member.summary: Summary statistics over one value column. Rows without a value are skipped, so is the number of values actually reduced. is the population standard deviation (divide by n), as for C-O statistics. is the raw median of absolute deviations from the median, not scaled to estimate a normal sigma.
member.remarks: An angle column is unwrapped about its circular mean before it is reduced, so 359° and 1° have a mean of 0° and a sigma of 1° rather than 180° and 179°. The mean lies in the column's wrap range. Min, median and max are on the same unwrapped scale, so they keep their order and can fall just outside the range (−1° … 1°). When the directions cancel out (0° and 180°) there is no mean direction and every statistic except the count is absent.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.MotionAlignmentAnalyzer
member.summary: Suggests the time offset that best lines up the motion of two angle series, such as a computed (prism-derived) angle and the observed sensor angle, by minimising the scatter of their difference across offsets: the cross-correlation peak, read in degrees. It reads the series it is given and changes nothing. The operator decides whether to set the suggestion as the attempt's match offset.
member.remarks: pairs timestamps only, so it finds gross clock errors but not a latency smaller than the sampling interval. This compares values, so it finds that latency to a small fraction of a sample, provided the vessel moves. The offset follows the matcher's convention (compared time + offset = reference time), with the reference as series A and the compared series as B.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.MotionAlignmentAnalyzer.MinimumSamples
member.summary: The fewest samples a series, or one offset's pairing, needs to be scored.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.MotionAlignmentAnalyzer.MinimumExcitationDegrees
member.summary: Below this standard deviation of the reference angle, in degrees, there is too little motion to line up.
member.remarks: Low enough for a moored vessel's yaw, a few hundredths of a degree, yet several times the scatter that millimetre prism noise leaves on a computed angle. A fit to noise alone is still flagged as weakly correlated.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.MotionAlignmentAnalyzer.MinimumCorrelation
member.summary: Below this correlation at the suggested offset, the motion may be noise rather than shared.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.MotionAlignmentAnalyzer.MinimumOverlapFraction
member.summary: An offset pairing fewer than this fraction of the reference samples is not scored at all: a short overlap can happen to scatter less than the whole record does at the right offset, without meaning anything.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.MotionAlignmentAnalyzer.SparseOverlapFraction
member.summary: Below this fraction of the reference samples paired at the suggested offset, the overlap is sparse.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.MotionAlignmentAnalyzer.AmbiguityContrast
member.summary: A rival offset whose scatter rises above the best by less than this fraction of the curve's depth (its median scatter less the best) makes the suggestion ambiguous.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.MotionAlignmentAnalyzer.OppositeMotionRatio
member.summary: When reversing the compared angle's sign would leave less than this fraction of the best offset's scatter, the series move opposite to each other.

member.name: F:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.MotionAlignmentAnalyzer.SessionGap
member.summary: The run of computed samples that a search lines up continues across a dropout shorter than this, and ends at a longer one. A brief loss of lock therefore stays in the surveyed window, while a separate session does not.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.MotionOffsetScorer
member.summary: Scores an offset by the scatter of reference − compared once the compared series is shifted by it: the standard deviation, in degrees, of what would become the C-O. Each reference sample is paired with the compared series linearly interpolated at the shifted time, so the two series may be sampled at different, uneven rates.

remarks.para: Minimising var(r − c) = var(r) + var(c) − 2 cov(r, c) is maximising the cross-covariance, so this finds the cross-correlation peak. Unlike a raw correlation it ignores the constant bias between the series (the C-O itself) and reads in degrees.

Both series are prepared once: timestamped samples sorted by time (the first of any duplicate time kept), unwrapped along time so a heading swinging through north stays continuous, and held as flat arrays. Each offset is then one allocation-free pass over both, so a fine search over long series stays fast. The arithmetic is in : the scorer only chooses an offset, and the C-O an operator accepts is still computed exactly from the matched pairs.

member.name: M:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.MotionOffsetScorer.AroundPairedRun(System.TimeSpan,System.TimeSpan,System.TimeSpan)
member.summary: A scorer over only the reference samples that matter for a search around . That is the largest run of reference samples that pair at the centre, widened by on either side so an offset up to that far away can still pair all of it. Excitation and the overlap an offset needs are measured over the run's paired samples. That way, motion elsewhere in a long record, or a long record compared with a short one, cannot decide the search. A run continues across a dropout shorter than (or three reference sampling intervals, if longer) and ends at a longer one. Returns this scorer when no run with the minimum number of samples pairs at the centre.

member.name: M:geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.SeriesMatcher.Match``2(geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.DataSeries{``0},geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.DataSeries{``1},geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.SeriesMatchConfiguration,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Match two series using . Both series must expose keys compatible with the chosen strategy (timestamps for and , index strings for the index strategies).

Pairs samples one-to-one whose keys from and are equal, ignoring case. When several B samples share a key, only the first can pair. Pairs and unmatched A samples come out in series A's order, and unmatched B samples in series B's order.

Pairs rows one-to-one by time, closest first: every pair of rows within is a candidate, and candidates are claimed in order of their gap, then series A's time order, then series B's, so equal gaps always resolve the same way. Pairs come out in series A's time order.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.GnssCheck.GnssComparisonBasis
member.summary:
The guarded comparison behind every GNSS spot check. It decides whether the reference and observed series can be differenced in the attempt's comparison frame, and which of them must first be transformed into it.
A Defined series in a different CRS or epoch from the frame is marked for transformation. The transformation itself runs outside the domain, through the coordinate transform service, and its provenance is attached with . Unspecified means the operator chose to assume the other side's CRS. It is accepted but flagged, and it is the only case in which positions are differenced without a stated frame. A Missing reference is refused.
The settled frame is checked against what PROJ says about it (the frameDescription argument of ). Without that, it is checked against its catalogue definition (the resolve argument). A frame whose horizontal axes are not in metres is refused, and so is a dynamic frame without a coordinate epoch. A datum ensemble is compared but flagged with its accuracy. A frame that neither source knows is compared as a label, and the summary says so.

member.name: M:geoDC.Domain.GnssCheck.GnssComparisonBasis.Assess(geoDC.Measurements.CrsReference,geoDC.Measurements.CrsReference,geoDC.Measurements.CrsReference,System.Func{geoDC.Measurements.CrsReference,geoDC.Domain.Crs.CrsDefinition},geoDC.Domain.Crs.CrsDescription)
member.summary: Settles the frame the series are compared in, whether they can be compared, and which must be transformed first. A Missing reference anywhere means a refusal. An Unspecified comparison frame takes the frame of whichever series is Defined, trying the reference series first. A series in the frame's CRS at a different stated epoch is refused, because moving positions in time needs a velocity model, which a transformation does not apply.
member.param: The attempt's comparison frame.
The reference series' CRS reference.
The observed series' CRS reference.
Optional catalogue lookup for the settled frame's definition, consulted when there is no .
What PROJ says about the settled frame. It decides the metre check. Ignored when it describes another reference.
member.returns: The verdict, settled frame and summary. A refusal is returned, not thrown.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.Instruments.DeviceProfileCatalogueReader
member.summary: Reads a from its JSON document. The document defines its attitude and position conventions, sources and provenance notes once, and each entry refers to them by id, so a value shared by several entries or axes is written and reviewed in one place. Enum values are kebab-case (bow-up, counter-clockwise), alignments use the stored tokens (correction-offset, error-subtracted, mount-angle/vessel-to-sensor, mount-angle/sensor-to-vessel), and an unknown property, a missing one or a dangling reference is an error.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.ShoreControl.ShoreControlDivergence
member.summary: The three-way comparison behind push, pull and ignore. Each link remembers the store revision the job last agreed with, called the base. A side has changed when its point's signature differs from the base's. The signature combines the lifecycle word, the active revision's content hash and the descriptor hash. A decommission, removal or re-description therefore counts as a change just as a re-observation does, while the same values entered on both sides count as no change at all.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.ShoreControl.ShoreControlJobCopies
member.summary: Finds the copy of shore control a job uses. A job has one current copy: its newest unlocked snapshot or, when every snapshot it holds is locked by approved results, its newest locked one. When two snapshots were taken at the same instant, the one with the later id wins, so the choice does not depend on load order. Older locked snapshots stay in the project with the values their results used. The app's pages and the job report both use this rule to read a job's shore control.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.ShoreControl.ShoreControlPoint
member.summary: A physical shore control mark (a nail in a quay, a bolt on a bollard) with a stable identity that outlives any job or project. Its position comes from its revisions: is the current statement and the rest are history. The point itself holds what does not change with a re-observation: name, description, station type, registry link, and the Active → Decommissioned lifecycle. Removing a point from a set leaves a tombstone instead of deleting the row, so a sync can tell "deleted here" from "never existed".

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.ShoreControl.ShoreControlSnapshot
member.summary:
A job's own copy of a shore control set. The project must hold every input its results came from, so a job does not read the shared store at computation time. Instead it takes a snapshot. The snapshot is an ordinary stored in the project (, with its own ids), plus a sync ledger. The ledger records the store set the snapshot stands for, the metadata revision the job last agreed with, one per point, and the full CRS definitions the set references.
Local work goes through like any set. Changes between the two sides are explicit: compares the local set, the ledger and the store three ways, and the operator pushes, pulls or ignores each point. A snapshot with no store identity is detached (imported or entered in the job) until saves it. A snapshot that has fed approved results is locked (). Pulls into it are refused, so those results cannot change silently, and newer shore control goes into a fresh snapshot.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.VesselFrame.BaselineAlignmentSolver
member.summary: Aligns the VRF to surveyed point-pair baselines with a constrained best-fit rotation about the origin. The primary baseline is turned exactly onto its nominated axis by the smallest rotation that does so. The one remaining degree of freedom, the rotation about that axis, is then chosen to minimise Σ |eᵢ − R·ûᵢ|² over the secondary baselines (unit direction ûᵢ, nominated axis eᵢ), equally weighted. That minimum has the closed form θ = atan2(B, A), so the same inputs always give the same solution.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.VesselFrame.CrpOriginPin
member.summary:
Guards the CRP origin invariant: the current primary member of the reference-frame feature group (the CRP) sits at the VRF origin, so its resolved state is always exactly (0,0,0). cannot enforce this alone, because it does not know whether its feature is the primary member. The writers that have both the primary flag and the state in scope call these guards instead.
Only the VRF transformation workflow moves the origin, so is exempt from these guards. A translation re-zeroes against the new origin because of how the applied delta is built, and a rotation pivots about the origin, so it leaves the CRP at (0,0,0).
The Check* methods return the violation message (or null) for pre-checks that show it as a notification. The Ensure* methods throw the same message for writers that enforce it.

member.name: T:geoDC.Domain.VesselFrame.ReferenceFrame
member.summary: The vessel reference frame. Positions in it are stored in GEOdc Standard axes (+X forward, +Y starboard, +Z down), regardless of what the vessel calls its own axes. records the vessel's own axis directions for display only. The origin is always (0,0,0), where the Common Reference Point sits (the primary member of the reference-frame feature group). Moving the origin to a different point is done through a VRF translation, not by editing this entity. A vessel has at most one reference frame, and it is edited in place because frames are not versioned.
